system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m). | Higher cap, ideally 50–100% for business warranties, with separate uncapped/price-capped fundamental, tax and indemnity claims. | **Reject as sole cap; negotiate category-specific caps** — 20% may be inadequate for concentrated customer, regulatory and IP risks. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k deductible basket. | Lower de minimis and basket, or at least an aggregate/tipping basket; no application to tax, title, fundamental warranties, indemnities or fraud. | **Narrow and carve out key claims** — the deductible formulation leaves Buyer bearing the first AUD 250k of loss. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | All claims notified within 18 months; Seller seeks this to apply broadly. | General warranties: at least 24 months; tax: through statutory limitation period plus buffer; fundamental/title: 6 years or statutory period; privacy/IP as appropriate to risk. | **Reject universal 18-month limit** — latent tax, title, IP and regulatory exposures may emerge later. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general cap and time limit. | Fundamental warranties (including title, capacity, authority and ownership) subject to a separate 100% price cap and longer period; title preferably uncapped or capped at price plus enforcement costs. | **Reject** — Buyer needs meaningful recourse if it does not receive the shares or valid authority to sell them. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Broad limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language purportedly apply to all claims; no stated fraud exception. | Express carve-out preserving claims for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and deliberate concealment, and preventing contractual exclusion of them. | **Insert express fraud carve-out** — no limitation or sole-remedy clause should protect dishonest conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Deems all facts in the indexed data room, accounts, registers and public records disclosed. | Specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties, with sufficient detail to identify nature and scope; data-room disclosure only if indexed, frozen, complete and expressly cross-referenced. | **Reject blanket general disclosure** — it improperly shifts the burden of finding and interpreting risks to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for anything known by Buyer/advisers or discoverable from data room/public records. | Limit knowledge exclusion to actual knowledge of named senior Buyer deal personnel, evidenced in writing, and exclude constructive/deemed knowledge. | **Reject “discoverable” and adviser knowledge** — it creates an unworkably broad warranty escape route. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller says reasonable endeavours and written consent delivery address the issue; no final consent or satisfaction of conditions is provided. Bluefen represents about AUD 3.6m/30% FY26 revenue. | Completion condition requiring unconditional written consent and satisfaction/waiver of all conditions; no material adverse amendments; termination/right to walk or price protection if unavailable. | **Make it a Buyer-benefit CP** — loss or impairment of this customer would be material. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approx. AUD 3.2m debt/security to be released after Completion. | Debt repaid and all security, guarantees and encumbrances irrevocably released at or before Completion, funded from Seller proceeds; delivery of payoff letter and releases as Completion deliverables. | **Reject post-Completion release** — debt-free/cash-free requires Buyer to acquire the company free of financial indebtedness and security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420k conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; no treatment of payroll tax, super or other on-costs. | Treat all bonuses and associated employment costs as Seller leakage/debt-like items or specifically indemnify; deduct/escrow sufficient amount at Completion. | **Require a Completion adjustment or indemnity** — Buyer should not fund transaction-triggered employee liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; AUD 180k remains open and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is provided. | Specific indemnity for all loss from defective/non-transfer of IP, plus delivery of paid-up evidence, assignment/confirmation and release before Completion; outside general limitations. | **Expand and ring-fence the indemnity** — ownership of core project materials is unverified and may be conditional on payment. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary incident; possible unintended disclosure of ~1,240 records; no confirmed access, scope, notification obligation or quantified loss; Seller says not expected material. | A specific indemnity, remediation covenant, ongoing investigation/reporting, access to evidence, notification/cooperation controls and adequate retention/escrow; warranty cover not qualified by materiality. | **Do not accept the materiality conclusion** — privacy exposure can crystallise after Completion even where access is initially uncertain. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110k renewals (AUD 330k aggregate) characterised as ordinary-course costs; disclosure does not establish avoidability, terms or accrual. | Full contracts and confirmation of term, termination rights, payment status and approval; treat unusual/prepaid/non-terminable commitments as leakage/debt-like or require Buyer consent. | **Seek facts and protection before accepting ordinary-course treatment** — the aggregate commitment may burden the post-Completion business. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller seeks one limitation/reliance/exclusive-remedy regime for all claims, notwithstanding different risk types; its “[STANDARD]” labels ask Buyer not to scrutinise terms. | Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, restrictive covenants, fraud and Completion obligations. | **Reject the unified regime and ignore Seller labelling** — risk allocation must follow claim type, not Seller’s administrative convenience. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller holds 100%; no confirmation of independent verification. | Completion deliverables: original share certificates (or indemnity), executed transfers, board approvals, updated register, no encumbrance releases, ASIC/company searches and title warranty. | **Require documentary Completion protection** — a register extract alone does not establish clean, transferable and unencumbered title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller treats tax and IP warranties as settled under the general regime. | Standalone tax covenant/indemnity, tax warranty package and long survival; robust IP warranties plus targeted Ironquay protection, with separate caps/survival. | **Reopen both categories** — tax and IP liabilities are specialised, potentially material and unsuitable for the general warranty regime. |
=== END ADVICE ===
